claim: Human fingernails and toenails continue to actively grow for several weeks following biological death.
context_passage: Biological nail growth requires sustained cellular division in the nail germinal matrix, driven by glucose metabolism and blood perfusion. When a human dies, cellular metabolism ceases immediately. The visual illusion that fingernails grow after death occurs because the surrounding skin and soft tissue undergo postmortem dehydration and desiccation, causing the skin to pull back and expose more nail length.

claim: Atmospheric lightning discharges produce natural nitrogen oxide compounds that fertilize plant life.
context_passage: During a lightning discharge, air temperatures inside the lightning channel exceed 30,000 Kelvin. This extreme thermal energy splits diatomic atmospheric nitrogen (N2) and oxygen (O2) molecules, allowing them to bond into nitric oxide (NO) and nitrogen dioxide (NO2). These gases react with rain precipitation to form nitrates and nitric acid, which fall to soil as naturally bioavailable nitrogen fertilizer.
